name: Fortnox
description: Fortnox — the Swedish SMB accounting standard: customers, invoices, supplier invoices, articles, orders, vouchers and the account chart. REST API v3, OAuth 2.0.
instructions:
**Getting a token**
1. Register at the **Fortnox Developer Portal** and create an integration. You receive a **client id** and **client secret**.
2. Run the authorization-code flow once for the customer's Fortnox account, asking for the scopes you need — `invoice`, `customer`, `article`, `order`, `supplierinvoice`, `bookkeeping`, `settings`. Keep the **refresh token**.
3. Set `FORTNOX_CLIENT_ID`, `FORTNOX_CLIENT_SECRET` and `FORTNOX_REFRESH_TOKEN`. AnythingMCP refreshes the access token on its own.

**The legacy Access-Token header is gone.** Fortnox retired the old `Access-Token` + `Client-Secret` header pair; if you find an example using those, it is pre-2022 and will not work. OAuth 2.0 is the only path now.

**Refresh tokens rotate.** Fortnox issues a new refresh token on every refresh and invalidates the old one. AnythingMCP persists the rotated value back into the connector — but sharing one refresh token between this connector and another script will break one of them.

**Rate limit** is roughly 25 requests per 5 seconds per token, answered with 429. Pace bulk work.

**Responses wrap the rows** in the resource name: `{"Customers": [...], "MetaInformation": {...}}`. The paging totals live in `MetaInformation` (`@TotalPages`, `@TotalResources`).

**`financialyear` matters for vouchers.** Fortnox scopes bookkeeping to a financial year id; without one it uses the current year, which is a surprise in January.

**Cloud reachability**: api.fortnox.se is public with a valid certificate.

tools.name: fortnox_get_company_settings
tools.description: Read the connected company's settings: name, organisation number, VAT number, address and currency. The fastest proof that the OAuth client works.

tools.name: fortnox_list_customers
tools.description: List customers with their number, name, organisation number, address and payment terms. Filter by name or organisation number to find one.

filter.description: Named filter, e.g. active or inactive.

organisationnumber.description: Exact organisation number to look up.

tools.name: fortnox_get_customer
tools.description: Read one customer by their customer number, with addresses, delivery defaults, VAT settings and price list.

tools.name: fortnox_list_invoices
tools.description: List invoices with their number, date, due date, customer, total and balance. Filter `unpaidoverdue` answers 'who is late' directly.

filter.description: Named filter: cancelled, fullypaid, unpaid, unpaidoverdue, unbooked.

tools.name: fortnox_get_invoice
tools.description: Read one invoice in full: every row with article, quantity, price and VAT, the totals, the payment terms and the balance outstanding.

tools.name: fortnox_list_supplier_invoices
tools.description: List supplier invoices with their supplier, date, due date, total and payment state — the payables side of the ledger.

filter.description: Named filter: cancelled, fullypaid, unpaid, unpaidoverdue, unbooked.

tools.name: fortnox_list_orders
tools.description: List sales orders with their number, customer, date, delivery state and total, for the pipeline between quote and invoice.

filter.description: Named filter: cancelled, expired, invoicecreated, invoicenotcreated.

tools.name: fortnox_list_articles
tools.description: List articles with their number, description, sales price, purchase price, stock quantity and unit.

articlenumber.description: Exact article number to look up.

tools.name: fortnox_list_vouchers
tools.description: List bookkeeping vouchers in a financial year with their series, number, date and description — the ledger underneath the documents.

financialyear.description: Financial year id. Omitted, Fortnox uses the current year — a surprise in January.

tools.name: fortnox_list_accounts
tools.description: List the chart of accounts for a financial year with each account's number, description, VAT code and balance-carry setting.
